name: Claude Code
use_case: Make a bounded repository change while tracking coding-agent usage
audience: Terminal-oriented builders who can review diffs and run project tests
verdict: A researched candidate for a scoped edit/test/review loop. Use /usage to inspect consumption; do not confuse an API cost estimate with a subscription invoice.
tradeoff: Gateway retries and permission fixes are vendor-reported, not independently tested. Monitor availability now extends to Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry, with long foreground sleeps blocked there too; verify scripts and denial behavior on your own provider before upgrading production.
privacy: Review repository and tool permissions, exclude secrets, and inspect provider data terms before sending private source. Human review remains necessary.
pricing: Checked 2026-10-26 in official costs docs: API use is token-billed; Pro/Max subscribers have included usage subject to plan limits. /usage session dollars estimate API list-price consumption, not subscription billing. No fixed subscription price verified in this run; consult linked plan pricing before buying.
news: v2.1.310 published October 23: Monitor tools extend to Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry; fixes address gateway compatibility, dense-context compaction and Windows hook permission handling. Workflow: use an isolated repository, run a bounded change through your existing gateway, review symlink prompts and hook denial behavior, then compare test results before adopting. Vendor notes only; no gateway or agent execution performed.

name: VibeiDE
use_case: Queue and review several local coding agents without losing task history
audience: Builders already using Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode across projects
verdict: New, unranked candidate when terminal juggling becomes a problem; start with one read-only task before enabling parallel writes. A queue is not filesystem isolation.
tradeoff: Paid orchestration on top of separate provider costs. Select independent worktrees yourself. Maker reports full validation on macOS; Windows support has narrower validation and Linux is experimental. Not installed or benchmarked here.
privacy: Maker says task history is local and credentials stay with installed CLIs, but prompts reach your model provider. Account/licence checks require connectivity; optional mobile transport has separate boundaries. Local does not mean offline or no data egress.
pricing: Checked 2026-10-27: 14-day device-bound trial, no card. Solo $7.99 USD/month or $79/year; lifetime $249 once; Team $14.99/seat/month, before tax. Launch offers end January 1, 2027 00:00 UTC; new recurring prices then $9.99/month, $99/year and $19.99/seat/month; lifetime sale ends. Active subscriptions retain starting price. Provider usage/subscriptions extra; checkout not tested.
news: New to this catalog, not a verified new launch: official downloads advertise Desktop 0.8.21; no original release date established. Product guide reviewed October 21 describes per-project queues and completion review. Workflow: select a scratch checkout, ask one installed agent to identify entry point and test command, then verify both before allowing edits. Parallel write tasks need separate worktrees.
